title: Prepare source package and upload to Launchpad PPA
input: A developer wants to distribute an application on Ubuntu 24.04 via a Launchpad Personal Package Archive (PPA). What steps are required to build the source package, sign it, and upload it via dput?
evidence_requirements: Generation of source-only upload via debuild -S or dpkg-buildpackage -S -sa
Signing the source changes file with a GPG key registered on Launchpad
Uploading the package using dput ppa:<user>/<ppa> <package>_source.changes

title: Audit Ubuntu delta against upstream Debian package
input: An Ubuntu maintainer is updating a package synced from Debian. The current Ubuntu package version is `2.1.0-1ubuntu2` and Debian has released `2.1.0-2`. How should the maintainer inspect the existing delta, decide what to keep, and version the new Ubuntu release?
evidence_requirements: Inspection of delta using ubuntu-diff or debdiff
Identification of whether Ubuntu-specific patches were merged into Debian 2.1.0-2
Proper Ubuntu versioning (2.1.0-2ubuntu1) if delta remains, or direct sync if delta is eliminated

title: Structure a Stable Release Update (SRU) bug report and test plan
input: A severe bug in network-manager causes WiFi connection drops on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (Noble). A fix is ready in the development release. What formal documentation must accompany the SRU bug report for the Ubuntu SRU team?
evidence_requirements: Mandatory SRU sections: [Impact], [Test Plan], [Where problems could occur]
Detailed step-by-step test plan demonstrating reproduction of failure and verification of fix
Requirement for package to spend mandatory 7 days in noble-proposed before release to noble-updates

title: Diagnose Launchpad upload rejection due to invalid distribution suite
input: A maintainer builds a package for Ubuntu and uploads it to Launchpad via dput, but Launchpad sends a rejection email: `Rejected: Distribution 'unstable' is not supported on Launchpad`. What caused this and how is it fixed?
evidence_requirements: Identification that debian/changelog targeted Debian 'unstable' instead of an Ubuntu series codename
Updating debian/changelog to target the specific series (e.g., 'noble' or 'jammy')
Rebuilding the source package and re-uploading via dput

title: Diagnose Launchpad build failure on 32-bit armhf due to 64-bit time_t transition
input: A C application compiles cleanly on amd64 and arm64 in Launchpad, but fails on Ubuntu 24.04 armhf with `error: format '%ld' expects argument of type 'long int', but argument has type 'time_t {aka long long int}'`. What caused this failure?
evidence_requirements: Identification of Ubuntu 24.04 / Debian 64-bit time_t transition (t64) for Year 2038 compliance on 32-bit architectures
Explanation that time_t is now 64-bit (long long) on armhf
Fixing code by using appropriate format specifiers or explicit type casting

title: Resolve merge conflict between new Debian upstream and Ubuntu delta
input: When running `git ubuntu merge` or `merge-changelog` to rebase an Ubuntu delta on a new Debian release, conflicts arise in debian/control and debian/rules. What principles govern resolving the conflict?
evidence_requirements: Obligation to minimize delta by upstreaming changes back to Debian whenever possible
Careful preservation of genuine Ubuntu-specific requirements (AppArmor profiles, Mir/Wayland transitions, launchpad paths)
Documentation of the merge rationale and remaining delta in debian/changelog
